newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary f.min sees chance for devaluation rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Hungary f.min sees chance for devaluation rate cut.

text.p: Hungary should reduce its monthly 1.1 percent devaluation rate for the second half of the year if the current inflation and foreign trade trends in the economy continue, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said on Monday.
"If everything keeps going on as now, the devaluation rate can be, and I think, should be reduced for the second half of the year," Medgyessy told Reuters in an interview.
He added that a reduction was dependent on inflation and trade account trends.
"If the trade account's position is very bad, I would not regard a devaluation rate cut good," Medgyessy said.
Analysts and government officials have said that increasing economic growth may widen Hungary's trade deficit this year.
Hungary targets a gross domestic product (GDP) growth of two to three percent for 1997, up from a preliminary figure of one percent in 1996.
Medgyessy said the trade deficit figures for the first months of the year were better than expected.
Hungary posted a trade deficit of $431.4 million in the January-February period according to customs statistics.

Hungary will easily finance from foreign direct investments if the trade gap increases to $3 billion from $2.7 billion lasy year, Medgyessy said, adding that the trade deficit was not likely to exceed $3 billion.
Medgyessy said inflation trends also justified a cut in the devaluation rate.

He added that year-on-year inflation could go down to between 16 to 17 percent by December 1997 from 18.8 percent in March, adding that he would be able to give a more justified forecast in June, after seeing the May CPI figures.
Medgyessy said he did not expect year-on-year inflation to go up substantially in any month of this year.

"It is unlikely that we will see surprising peaks this year," he said, adding, however, that fruit prices were likely to push the price indices upward and tomato, potato and paprika prices may have the same impact.
